pages.title: Quickstart
pages.description: Install BetterShape, open a folder, and send one task.
pages.body: BetterShape is a desktop app. You open a project folder, describe the work in chat, and review the edits before they stay. 1. Go to GitHub releases. 2. Run the installer. 3. Open BetterShape from the Start menu. BetterShape needs Windows 10 or 11, 64 bit. If Windows SmartScreen appears, choose More info , then Run anyway . Open Settings → Providers and paste an API key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI compatible endpoint. Keys are stored on this machine and used only for your own requests. You can open files and edit without a key. Chat needs one, and tells you in the composer when none is configured. Use Open folder (or Ctrl+K then Ctrl+O ) and pick the project you want to work on. BetterShape stays in that folder until you open a different one. Chat, search, and Git all run against this folder. Open the repo root, not a nested package, unless you only want that package in context. Type in the composer at the bottom of chat. Start small so you can see how BetterShape edits files. Examples that work well: “Rename the primary button on the home page to Get started.” “Explain app/page.tsx in a few sentences.” “Add a loading state to the settings save button.” Press Enter to send. BetterShape reads the project, answers in the thread, and may edit files. Type @ and pick a file. That file is attached to the message. Use this when you already know which file matters, instead of hoping BetterShape finds it. Type / to run a saved prompt. See slash commands. When BetterShape edits a file, the diff shows in the thread. Keep the change if it matches what you asked. Skip it if it is wrong or too broad. Ask a follow up if it is close. Nothing is committed for you. When you want a commit, see Commits. The composer has a mode switch. Use Code for edits. Use Ask when you only want an explanation. Use Plan for a larger change. Use Review when something is broken. Details are on Agent. Pick the model from the composer's model menu. Everything your key can reach is available. See Models.

pages.title: Models
pages.description: Add your own provider keys and pick any model they offer.
pages.body: Every message uses a model. You pick it from the model menu in chat. Open Settings → Providers and paste an API key for the provider you use: Providers are grouped in the settings page, and the search box filters by name, group, or any model a provider serves. Group Providers Native APIs OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI, Azure OpenAI Gateways OpenRouter, OpenCode Zen, NVIDIA NIM, Vercel AI Gateway, LLM Gateway, ZenMux, Kilo Code, Cloudflare AI Gateway Providers xAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Mistral, Cerebras, Together AI, Fireworks AI, Moonshot (Kimi), Z.ai and Z.ai Coding Plan, Alibaba Qwen, DeepInfra, Venice, MiniMax, Baseten, DigitalOcean Gradient, Cohere, Perplexity, Cloudflare Workers AI, Databricks Local Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, and any other OpenAI compatible endpoint xAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Mistral, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google run on their own protocols; everything else in that list speaks the OpenAI wire format and differs only by base URL. Chat works as soon as one provider is enabled with a key. Without one, BetterShape says so instead of failing mid turn. Providers without keys — Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, and OpenCode Zen's free models — ship turned off , so a fresh install never sends a request anywhere you did not choose. Enable the card and they route with no key. Test connection asks the provider for its model list with the key and base URL currently in the card. A green answer means the key works and the endpoint is right; the app then offers Use these N models to import the ids your account actually serves. This works before you save, and it is the fastest way to pin down a wrong base URL or a key that belongs to another provider. Check chat goes one step further and sends one short completion through the same translation layer the agent uses. That is what proves a model answers — a gateway can list models and still reject completions because of a missing header, the wrong auth header, or a model slug the account cannot use. Keys are kept in your OS keychain, not in the app's settings file. Header values are stored there too, because gateways put tokens in headers. Some gateways want more than a bearer token. Open Request headers & auth on a provider card to set: Auth header — where the key travels: Authorization: Bearer (default), api key (Azure OpenAI), x api key (Anthropic compatible endpoints), x goog api key , or none at all for a self hosted server. Extra headers — one Name: value per line, e.g. X Tenant: acme , or cf aig authorization: Bearer for a Cloudflare AI Gateway. Preset headers appear on the card: OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, Vercel AI Gateway, LLM Gateway, ZenMux and Kilo Code receive the attribution headers their own clients send, and NVIDIA NIM additionally gets X BILLING INVOKE ORIGIN . Your lines win over a preset's, and the app identifies itself as bettershape/ on every request. Every request also carries the model id's prefix, so a provider/model id always lands on the provider you configured. Aliases from other clients ( gemini/… , opencode zen/… , kimi/… , nvidia nim/… ) resolve to the connections on this app's list. The model menu lists the models your key can reach, plus anything extra you add by hand. The default is Auto , which uses your first configured provider unless you set a different default in Settings → Providers . Model ids you paste from somewhere else keep working: a name listed by any configured provider is offered by its own card, and the app maps prefixes such as gemini/ or nvidia nim/ onto the connection they mean. Codebase search uses an OpenAI compatible /embeddings endpoint. OpenAI, OpenRouter, Mistral, Together AI, DeepInfra, NVIDIA NIM, Alibaba Qwen and the local runtimes offer known embedding models; anything else OpenAI wire needs the model id typed in (Ollama's nomic embed text , vLLM's BAAI/bge m3 ). Providers that cannot embed — Groq, xAI, DeepSeek — are skipped instead of being sent a model they do not serve. Turn embeddings off any time; keyword search and the file index still work. Image, speech, and caption tools need an OpenAI wire provider. They use the same key as chat. Your provider bills you directly. BetterShape shows the tokens spent on the last turn in the composer ring, not a credit balance. Client trust and provider keys Plugins

pages.title: Agent
pages.description: Chat with the open folder. BetterShape reads, answers, and can edit files.
pages.body: Chat sits next to your files. You describe the work. BetterShape reads the open folder, answers in the thread, and can edit files when you ask it to. You stay in control of what is kept. Every edit shows a diff. You still commit with Git when you want a commit. Switch the mode on the composer before you send. The mode applies to that message. Code edits files and can run commands. This is the default for building. Ask answers without changing the project. Use it to read a file, compare options, or explain an error. Plan writes the approach first and waits. See Plan. Visual works on UI. Describe the screen, or pair it with the in app browser. Review looks for a bug and proposes a small fix. See Review. If you send a Code request that is actually a question, BetterShape may still try to edit. Switch to Ask when you do not want files to move. Type @ and pick a file or folder. That path goes with the message. Use @ when: You already know the file. The name is common ( button.tsx exists in more than one place). You want BetterShape to stay inside one package of a monorepo. You can attach more than one. Keep the set small. Extra files add noise. Type / to run a slash command. Use this for work you repeat: a commit message, a PR checklist, a test pass. Every file edit shows a diff in the thread. 1. Read the diff. 2. Keep it, skip it, or say what to change. 3. Repeat until the thread is done. BetterShape does not push to GitHub on its own. See Commits when you want a commit. Start a new chat when the topic changes. A long thread about one bug will confuse a later request about a different feature. Ctrl+Shift+L opens a new chat. Chat can use a connected plugin (GitHub, Slack, Linear, and similar) or a local MCP server. Connect those first, then mention the task in the message.

pages.title: Plan
pages.description: Agree on the steps before BetterShape edits files.
pages.body: Use Plan when the work is large enough that you want to see the steps first. A rename in one file does not need Plan. A new settings page across several files does. Plan writes the approach into .bettershape/plans/ and shows it in the thread. It does not start editing until you continue. The plan is a file you can read and change. If a step is wrong, fix it in the thread before you build. 1. Switch the composer to Plan . 2. Describe the change in the same way you would in Code. Include the goal, the files you know about, and anything that must not change. 3. Wait for the plan in the thread. 4. Edit the plan if a step is off. Say which step and why. 5. Continue when you want BetterShape to build it. If you already know the change is one file, skip Plan and use Code. Good Plan prompts name the outcome and the limits: “Add a password field to account settings. Do not change billing.” “Split the homepage hero into its own component. Keep the current copy.” Weak prompts skip the limit. BetterShape will fill in the blanks, and you will spend a turn undoing that. Building uses the plan as the checklist. If the implementation drifts, say so in the same thread. Start a new Plan only if the goal itself changed. When the build is done, read the diffs the same way you would after Code. Keep or skip each file. Commit when you are ready. See Commits.

pages.title: Review
pages.description: Find the cause, then make a small fix.
pages.body: Use Review when something is broken, or when a change feels risky and you want a second look. It is not for rewriting a feature. The Review mark in the composer is the purple mask icon. There is no separate Debug mode. Review looks for the cause first, then proposes a small fix. You still keep or skip the diff. It works best when you give it a signal: A stack trace from the terminal. A failing test name. @ on the file that throws. The last change you made, in one sentence. “It doesn’t work” is not enough. BetterShape will guess, and the guess is often the wrong file. 1. Switch the composer to Review . 2. Paste the error or point at the file. 3. Read the finding in the thread. It should name the cause, not only restyle the code. 4. Keep the fix if it is small and correct. Skip it if it refactors past the bug. After a multi file change, you can run Review on the same thread and ask it to list what is actually wrong. That still lands as diffs you can keep or skip. Do not use Review as a formatter. If you want tests written, say that in Code . If you want a second pass on a pull request, say which PR. See GitHub.

pages.title: Browser
pages.description: Change the running page. The source updates with it.
pages.body: Use the in app browser when you want to edit the live page instead of describing the UI in chat. This is not the same as Visual mode in the composer. Visual mode asks the agent to design. The browser lets you click the page in front of you. 1. Run your app the way you usually do ( npm run dev , and so on). 2. Copy the local URL (for example http://localhost:3000 ). 3. Open that URL in BetterShape’s browser. This works with Next.js, Vite, Astro, and Remix. The app has to be running. BetterShape does not start it for you. If the preview cannot reach localhost, the dev server is not up, or it is bound to another host. See troubleshooting. Select an element and change it. BetterShape writes the same change into the source. You still review the diff in the thread. Keep it if the source matches what you changed on the page. Skip it if it touched the wrong file. Layout and copy changes map cleanly when the element is in one component. Shared components update every screen that uses them. That is correct. Read the diff before you keep it. Styles that come from a design token may change the token, not a one off class. You can still send a Visual or Code message while the browser is open. Say which screen you have open if the app has more than one route. When you are done, go back to Code for logic that is not on the page.

pages.title: Context and compaction
pages.description: How a long thread stays inside the model's context window.
pages.body: Every turn re sends the whole thread to the model: your messages, the agent's answers, and every tool result. The context window is finite, so a long thread runs out of room eventually. Input gets truncated, and BetterShape seems to forget what you said an hour ago. A short chat never hits the limit. A long one does, and it helps to know what survives. 1. Tool output is trimmed. Old tool results shrink to a head and tail excerpt. A result the model no longer needs, such as an older read of a file it read again later, becomes a one line note. 2. Older turns are summarized. Past roughly 74% of the window, BetterShape folds the older turns into one summary and keeps the newest turns word for word. That is compaction. 3. The summary is reused. After the first fold, later turns send the summary plus the recent turns instead of the whole transcript, so BetterShape does not re summarize on every message. 4. Oversized output goes to disk. A single tool result too big for the budget is written under .bettershape/agent out/ and the model gets the path. Manual compaction uses the same engine as the automatic pass, so a thread you compacted by hand keeps working the same way. The agent can also compact mid task when a turn is running long. The summary follows a fixed outline rather than a free form recap: The request and the intent, including anything you ruled out. Technical concepts and the shape of the solution. Files and code sections, with the important snippets. Errors, fixes, and rejected approaches. Problems solved and the state of the work. Every user message, so early instructions survive. Work in progress and the next step. BetterShape also re attaches the five most recently read or written files, so the agent picks up where it left off instead of re reading them. Want every summary to carry something specific? An API shape, a set of migration names, a house tone? Write it once in Settings → Agents → Instructions → Compaction. Those instructions are appended to every compaction, manual or automatic. Automatic compaction picks its moment from a token count, and a token count cannot tell whether the agent is half way through a rename across six files. When it is, the agent can hold the automatic pass. It calls compact context on its own, with a one line reason: That call is the hold, not a summary of the work. The reason is pinned into the next summary, so the thing it was protecting survives the fold. A hold is bounded, because an unbounded one would let the window overflow, and a truncated window loses more than a summary does: It lapses after about 15 minutes, or 16k tokens of growth, or 3 skipped passes. It is overridden when the chat reaches about 92% of the window. It is checked before every model call in a turn, not only between turns. A single run of work can take hundreds of tool calls, and a window that fills up in the middle of one fails the call outright, so the check happens mid turn too. /compact from you always works, and a finished turn clears the hold. A fold is saved as it happens, so a summary survives a restart and a reopened chat does not send the raw history again. Only the part no summary covers yet is sent to be summarized, and the previous summary is handed in as the base. Settings → Agents → Context shows the hold, its reason, and a Compact now button while one is active. Compaction changes what the model reads, not what you keep. The earlier messages stay in the chat, with a marker where the summary took over. The pre compaction transcript is archived under .bettershape/agent out/ , so the agent can grep it when a detail is missing. Each chat keeps its own summary. Opening another thread, or starting a new one, starts from that thread's history. Settings → Agents → Context shows what compaction has done in the open chat: how many passes, how many tokens it freed. Reset goes back to sending the raw transcript, and since nothing was deleted, nothing is lost. Incognito chats are never summarized. If the summary call fails, or the result is too short to be useful, BetterShape leaves the thread alone and retries later. It will not silently drop turns. "Nothing to compact yet" means the thread is still small enough to send whole.

pages.title: Plugins
pages.description: Connect an outside account so chat can use it.
pages.body: Plugins let chat use GitHub, Slack, Linear, Stripe, and similar accounts. You connect the account once, then mention the task in a message. Plugins run through your own Composio account. Add its API key in Settings → Agents → Plugins first (composio.com → API keys). A tool that runs on your machine is MCP. 1. Open Settings → Agents → Plugins . 2. Pick the service. 3. Sign in in the browser window and allow access. 4. Return to BetterShape. You can disconnect from the same place. Disconnecting stops new chat turns from using that account. It does not delete past threads. Say what you need in plain language. You do not need a special syntax. Examples: “Open a pull request for this branch.” “List my Linear issues tagged bug.” “Post a summary of this diff to the engineering Slack channel.” If the plugin is not connected, BetterShape cannot call it. Connect it first, then send the message again. Signing in for GitHub loads pull requests and related data for the open folder. A GitHub plugin is for chat. You may need both, depending on what you are doing. Sign in again. Check that the account has access to the repo or workspace you named. Then send a shorter message that names the repo or channel.

pages.title: MCP
pages.description: Add a local tool server BetterShape can call from chat.
pages.body: MCP servers are tools BetterShape can call from chat. Add one in Settings → Agents → MCP , or keep a server in mcp.json if you want it in a file. Servers you add in Settings stay in BetterShape. They are not written into mcp.json . A server in mcp.json is picked up on its own. You do not have to add it again in Settings. Use MCP when the tool runs on your machine or at a URL you already have. Use a plugin when the tool is an outside account. Open Settings → Agents → MCP and choose Add server . There are two tabs. Browse the registry searches the official MCP registry, the same index the agent searches. Search for a product or package name, check the command shown under a result, then choose Install . BetterShape writes the entry to mcp.json and connects it, so the server is there after a restart. If it needs a sign in, BetterShape opens the browser flow. Paste a config takes a server URL or a JSON config. Servers added this way stay in BetterShape and are not written to mcp.json . Remove a server you added by pasting with Remove . That does not change mcp.json . On the MCP page, choose Open mcp.json . If the file does not exist yet, BetterShape creates it. Use command when BetterShape should start the process. Use url if the server is already running. Save the file. Name the server something you will recognize in chat. The name is what you will refer to, not the package name. Send a message that needs the tool. If the server does not show up: 1. Save mcp.json . 2. Open Settings → Agents → MCP again. BetterShape reloads the file. 3. Open the same folder again. 4. Check that command is on your PATH when BetterShape starts. A tool that only works in your existing terminal session will fail here. You do not have to open Settings for this. Ask in chat, and BetterShape can add, change, test, or remove a server for you. The tools are mcp manage (server lifecycle) and mcp search / mcp call (using the tools a server exposes). The agent can: List servers and their status. Search the registry for a server by name, then add it from the registry entry. Add, update, enable, disable, or remove a server, with command / args / env for a local process or url / headers for a remote one. Test a server and report the tool count and latency. A test that passes saves the server unless you pass save: false . Start sign in for a server that needs OAuth. List the tools a server exposes. Servers the agent creates are written to the same mcp.json the Settings page reads, so they show up there too. Pass save: false to add a server for the current session only. Adding a server changes which tools BetterShape can call, so a mode that only reads will not do it. Approve the action like any other edit. A local server is a program this machine will run, so the first time one is added, updated, or tested, BetterShape asks for approval in the chat and shows the exact command. Servers already in mcp.json , and everything you add yourself in Settings, are past that point. Set Auto run to Always in Settings to stop the questions. Remote servers that authenticate with a header use headers : BetterShape sends those headers on every request to that server. When the server uses OAuth instead, BetterShape does not send a stored Authorization header — the OAuth token wins. You do not have to open Settings for this. Ask in chat, and BetterShape can add, change, test, or remove a server for you. The tools are mcp manage (server lifecycle) and mcp search / mcp call (using the tools a server exposes). The agent can: List servers and their status. Search the registry for a server by name, then add it from the registry entry. Add, update, enable, disable, or remove a server, with command / args / env for a local process or url / headers for a remote one. Test a server and report the tool count and latency. A test that passes saves the server unless you pass save: false . Start sign in for a server that needs OAuth. List the tools a server exposes. Servers the agent creates are written to the same mcp.json the Settings page reads, so they show up there too. Pass save: false to add a server for the current session only. Adding a server changes which tools BetterShape can call, so a mode that only reads will not do it. Approve the action like any other edit. A local server is a program this machine will run, so the first time one is added, updated, or tested, BetterShape asks for approval in the chat and shows the exact command. Servers already in mcp.json , and everything you add yourself in Settings, are past that point. Set Auto run to Always in Settings to stop the questions. Remote servers that authenticate with a header use headers : BetterShape sends those headers on every request to that server. When the server uses OAuth instead, BetterShape does not send a stored Authorization header — the OAuth token wins. mcp.json lives in BetterShape’s data folder, not in the repo. Do not put API keys in it. Use env vars the server already reads. Delete the entry from mcp.json and save. Restart BetterShape if the tool still appears.

pages.title: Slash commands
pages.body: A slash command is a name plus a prompt you reuse. Type / in chat to pick one. Use this for work you do the same way every time: writing a commit message, checking a PR, generating tests in a fixed shape. 1. Open Settings → Agents → Workflows . 2. Give it a short name. That name is what you type after / . 3. Write the prompt you want BetterShape to follow. Be specific about the output: a commit message, a list of risks, a test file, and so on. 4. Save it. Keep the prompt as the instructions, not as a one off about the current branch. The current project still comes from the open folder and the thread. Type / in the composer and choose the command. You can add extra text after it, such as /commit focus on the billing page . A trigger phrase in a normal message can run it too, if you set one on the command. Write it like you would brief a person who has never seen this repo: What to look at ( @ files, or “the diff in source control”). What to produce. What to avoid (“do not change snapshots”). Bad commands are one word. “Review” with no standard is not a command. The Review mode already exists. Open Settings → Agents → Workflows again. Change the prompt, or delete the command. Existing threads do not change. Skills (reusable instructions the agent can load) live under Settings → Agents → Skills . They are separate from slash commands. BetterShape ships a few commands that are not prompts. They run locally and never reach the model. Command What it does /compact [focus] Summarize the earlier part of the thread and keep going. Long threads eventually fill the model's context window. /compact folds the older turns into one summary, keeps the newest turns verbatim, and continues in the same thread. Use it when: The thread is long and BetterShape starts forgetting things you said earlier. You finished a stage of work and want to start the next one without the old noise. A request failed because the context was too long. Add a focus to steer the summary: /compact keep the migration plan and the API shapes . Without a focus, BetterShape uses your standing compaction instructions from Settings → Agents → Instructions → Compaction . BetterShape also compacts on its own when a thread gets close to the window limit, so you rarely have to run this. The summary is the record of what was folded — everything before it stays in the transcript for you to scroll, and older turns are not deleted from the thread. See Context and compaction for what is kept and what is dropped.

pages.title: Commits
pages.description: Commit from chat, the terminal, or the graph.
pages.body: BetterShape does not commit when it edits a file. You keep or skip the diff in chat first. Then you commit what is actually on disk. In Code mode, ask it to commit. Name the files if you only want some of them. Read the message it drafts before you let it run. This uses the open folder’s git repo. Open the repo root, not a nested package, unless that package is its own repo. Open the terminal ( Ctrl+ ) and run git the way you usually do. Stage, commit, and push from there if you prefer. View → Git Manager opens the commit graph in the workspace. Use it to see history on the current folder. A GitHub login is only needed for remotes hosted on GitHub, pull requests, issues, and Actions. Local commits work without it. See GitHub. Keep or skip the diffs in the chat thread first. Then commit what is actually in the working tree. Skipping a diff in chat and committing the same file from disk will still include that file if it is still changed on disk.

pages.title: GitHub
pages.description: Pull requests, issues, and Actions for the open repo.
pages.body: Sign in with GitHub when the open folder has a github.com remote. This login is separate from the account you use for chat. A local only repo has nothing to load from GitHub. Open a pull request from the workspace, or ask chat after you connect the GitHub plugin. Finish the browser step, then return to BetterShape. If data is missing, sign in again, and confirm the open folder is the repo you think it is ( git remote v in the terminal). 1. Commit and push the branch. See Commits. 2. Open a pull request from BetterShape, or ask chat to open one if the GitHub plugin is connected. 3. Read the title and body. BetterShape can draft them from the branch. You confirm before it is published. Do not publish a PR for a folder that is not the repo you meant to open. Asking chat to “open a PR” uses a plugin if you connected one. GitHub login is for the open folder’s github.com remote. Use whichever matches the task. Sign out of GitHub from the same place you signed in. Chat is unaffected — it uses your model provider keys.

pages.title: Install
pages.body: BetterShape is a desktop app for Windows 10 or 11, 64 bit. There is no browser only editor. You download the app, then open a folder on disk. 1. Get the installer from GitHub releases. 2. Run it. 3. If Windows SmartScreen appears, choose More info , then Run anyway . 4. Open BetterShape from the Start menu. If the installer will not run, you are on 32 bit Windows, or the download was cut short. Download it again. There is no account to create and nothing to sign in to. BetterShape has no server of its own, so chat runs once you supply a model key yourself. 1. Open Settings , then Providers . 2. Add a key for OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google — or any OpenAI compatible endpoint. 3. Pick a default model under Settings , then AI . Until a usable provider is configured, the composer stays disabled and says so. Everything else — opening files, editing, git, terminal — works without one. This build has no update feed. Help → Check for Updates contacts no server. If you need a newer version, download a fresh installer from GitHub releases and run it over the existing install. Uninstall from Windows Settings like any other desktop app. Your project files on disk are not deleted. Local BetterShape data for the app may remain under your user folder. Open a folder and send a task.

pages.title: Shortcuts
pages.body: These are the defaults. Change them in Settings → Application → Keyboard Shortcuts . Action Shortcut Open folder Ctrl+K Ctrl+O Show or hide chat Ctrl+L New chat Ctrl+Shift+L Command palette Ctrl+Shift+P Go to file Ctrl+P Terminal Ctrl+ Settings Ctrl+, Design mode (in app browser) Ctrl+Shift+D Cycle Code / Ask / Plan Ctrl+Shift+. Open Settings → Application → Keyboard Shortcuts and assign a new chord. If the key is taken, pick another or clear the old one. Open folder is two steps: Ctrl+K , then Ctrl+O . Wait for the chord, then press the second part. If you only press Ctrl+K , you are waiting for the follow up. Ctrl+L shows or hides the chat sidebar. Click the composer (or start a new chat) when you want to type.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.body: Editing files, search, and the terminal work without a connection. Chat and Git push/pull need one. No. BetterShape has no account, no plan, and no credits. You pay your model provider directly for what you use. Not by default. Chat sends the files and context you include in a turn, plus what the agent reads to do the task. Local editing does not require chat. That is the only way chat works. Add a key in Settings → Providers — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI compatible endpoint. Nothing is proxied through a server we run. Windows 10 or 11, 64 bit. See Install. No. There is no BetterShape account. The only credentials in the app are the provider keys you add and the Git host login you use for push and pull.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: When install, keys, or chat fail.
pages.body: Start with the matching heading. If none of these fit, contact with the version from Help → About . It needs Windows 10 or 11, 64 bit. Download the installer again from GitHub releases and run it. If it opens and closes immediately, run it once more after a reboot. If it still fails, send the version you tried to install. Open Settings → Providers and add an API key. BetterShape calls the provider directly with that key; there is no account to sign in to. If a key is set and send still fails, the provider returned the error — the status line under the message names the provider and the HTTP status. The menu lists the models offered by presets, plus anything in Extra models on the provider card. Add the id by hand if your provider serves a model we do not list. Start your app first, then open that URL in the browser. localhost has to be the same machine. A URL on another device will not load in BetterShape’s preview. Sign in with GitHub and open a folder whose remote is on github.com. A fork or an org the GitHub account cannot see will look empty. Save mcp.json , restart BetterShape, and open the folder again. The command has to exist on PATH for the app, not only for a terminal you already opened. See MCP. Use Help → Check for Updates . This build has no update feed, so if it still reports the old version, install over it from GitHub releases.

pages.title: Contact
pages.body: Product questions go to contact. Include: The version from Help → About . What you tried, and what happened instead. Do not send API keys, provider tokens, or a dump of .env files. There is nothing to bill here: BetterShape has no account and no subscription. Model usage is billed by the provider whose key you added. Security issues go through SECURITY.md on GitHub. Do not file those as a normal product question. If a provider's API is down, check that provider's status page before you write in.

chunks.heading: Add a provider key
chunks.text: Open Settings → Providers and paste an API key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI compatible endpoint. Keys are stored on this machine and used only for your own requests. You can open files and edit without a key. Chat needs one, and tells you in the composer when none is configured.
chunks.title: Quickstart

chunks.heading: Open a folder
chunks.text: Use Open folder (or Ctrl+K then Ctrl+O ) and pick the project you want to work on. BetterShape stays in that folder until you open a different one. Chat, search, and Git all run against this folder. Open the repo root, not a nested package, unless you only want that package in context.
chunks.title: Quickstart

chunks.heading: Send a first task
chunks.text: Type in the composer at the bottom of chat. Start small so you can see how BetterShape edits files. Examples that work well: “Rename the primary button on the home page to Get started.” “Explain app/page.tsx in a few sentences.” “Add a loading state to the settings save button.” Press Enter to send. BetterShape reads the project, answers in the thread, and may edit files.
chunks.title: Quickstart

chunks.heading: Point it at a file
chunks.text: Type @ and pick a file. That file is attached to the message. Use this when you already know which file matters, instead of hoping BetterShape finds it. Type / to run a saved prompt. See slash commands.
chunks.title: Quickstart

chunks.heading: Review the diff
chunks.text: When BetterShape edits a file, the diff shows in the thread. Keep the change if it matches what you asked. Skip it if it is wrong or too broad. Ask a follow up if it is close. Nothing is committed for you. When you want a commit, see Commits.
chunks.title: Quickstart

chunks.heading: Pick a mode
chunks.text: The composer has a mode switch. Use Code for edits. Use Ask when you only want an explanation. Use Plan for a larger change. Use Review when something is broken. Details are on Agent.
chunks.title: Quickstart

chunks.heading: If chat will not send
chunks.text: Pick the model from the composer's model menu. Everything your key can reach is available. See Models.
chunks.title: Quickstart

chunks.text: Every message uses a model. You pick it from the model menu in chat.
chunks.title: Models

chunks.heading: Add a provider
chunks.text: Open Settings → Providers and paste an API key for the provider you use: Providers are grouped in the settings page, and the search box filters by name, group, or any model a provider serves. Group Providers Native APIs OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI, Azure OpenAI Gateways OpenRouter, OpenCode Zen, NVIDIA NIM, Vercel AI Gateway, LLM Gateway, ZenMux, Kilo Code, Cloudflare AI Gateway Providers xAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Mistral, Cerebras, Together AI, Fireworks AI, Moonshot (Kimi), Z.ai and Z.ai Coding Plan, Alibaba Qwen, DeepInfra, Venice, MiniMax, Baseten, DigitalOcean Gradient, Cohere, Perplexity, Cloudflare Workers AI, Databricks Local Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, and any other OpenAI compatible endpoint xAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Mistral, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google run on their own protocols; everything else in that list speaks the OpenAI wire format and differs only by base URL. Chat works as soon as one provider is enabled with a key. Without one, BetterShape says so instead of failing mid turn. Providers without keys — Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, and OpenCode Zen's free models — ship turned off , so a fresh install never sends a request anywhere you did not choose. Enable the card and they route with no key.
chunks.title: Models

chunks.heading: Verify a key
chunks.text: Test connection asks the provider for its model list with the key and base URL currently in the card. A green answer means the key works and the endpoint is right; the app then offers Use these N models to import the ids your account actually serves. This works before you save, and it is the fastest way to pin down a wrong base URL or a key that belongs to another provider. Check chat goes one step further and sends one short completion through the same translation layer the agent uses. That is what proves a model answers — a gateway can list models and still reject completions because of a missing header, the wrong auth header, or a model slug the account cannot use. Keys are kept in your OS keychain, not in the app's settings file. Header values are stored there too, because gateways put tokens in headers.
chunks.title: Models

chunks.heading: Request headers and auth
chunks.text: Some gateways want more than a bearer token. Open Request headers & auth on a provider card to set: Auth header — where the key travels: Authorization: Bearer (default), api key (Azure OpenAI), x api key (Anthropic compatible endpoints), x goog api key , or none at all for a self hosted server. Extra headers — one Name: value per line, e.g. X Tenant: acme , or cf aig authorization: Bearer for a Cloudflare AI Gateway. Preset headers appear on the card: OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, Vercel AI Gateway, LLM Gateway, ZenMux and Kilo Code receive the attribution headers their own clients send, and NVIDIA NIM additionally gets X BILLING INVOKE ORIGIN . Your lines win over a preset's, and the app identifies itself as bettershape/ on every request. Every request also carries the model id's prefix, so a provider/model id always lands on the provider you configured. Aliases from other clients ( gemini/… , opencode zen/… , kimi/… , nvidia nim/… ) resolve to the connections on this app's list.
chunks.title: Models

chunks.heading: Pick a model
chunks.text: The model menu lists the models your key can reach, plus anything extra you add by hand. The default is Auto , which uses your first configured provider unless you set a different default in Settings → Providers . Model ids you paste from somewhere else keep working: a name listed by any configured provider is offered by its own card, and the app maps prefixes such as gemini/ or nvidia nim/ onto the connection they mean.
chunks.title: Models

chunks.heading: Embeddings and search
chunks.text: Codebase search uses an OpenAI compatible /embeddings endpoint. OpenAI, OpenRouter, Mistral, Together AI, DeepInfra, NVIDIA NIM, Alibaba Qwen and the local runtimes offer known embedding models; anything else OpenAI wire needs the model id typed in (Ollama's nomic embed text , vLLM's BAAI/bge m3 ). Providers that cannot embed — Groq, xAI, DeepSeek — are skipped instead of being sent a model they do not serve. Turn embeddings off any time; keyword search and the file index still work.
chunks.title: Models

chunks.heading: Media
chunks.text: Image, speech, and caption tools need an OpenAI wire provider. They use the same key as chat.
chunks.title: Models

chunks.heading: Cost
chunks.text: Your provider bills you directly. BetterShape shows the tokens spent on the last turn in the composer ring, not a credit balance.
chunks.title: Models

chunks.heading: Related
chunks.text: Client trust and provider keys Plugins
chunks.title: Models

chunks.text: Chat sits next to your files. You describe the work. BetterShape reads the open folder, answers in the thread, and can edit files when you ask it to. You stay in control of what is kept. Every edit shows a diff. You still commit with Git when you want a commit.
chunks.title: Agent

chunks.heading: Modes
chunks.text: Switch the mode on the composer before you send. The mode applies to that message. Code edits files and can run commands. This is the default for building. Ask answers without changing the project. Use it to read a file, compare options, or explain an error. Plan writes the approach first and waits. See Plan. Visual works on UI. Describe the screen, or pair it with the in app browser. Review looks for a bug and proposes a small fix. See Review. If you send a Code request that is actually a question, BetterShape may still try to edit. Switch to Ask when you do not want files to move.
chunks.title: Agent

chunks.heading: Attach a file
chunks.text: Type @ and pick a file or folder. That path goes with the message. Use @ when: You already know the file. The name is common ( button.tsx exists in more than one place). You want BetterShape to stay inside one package of a monorepo. You can attach more than one. Keep the set small. Extra files add noise.
chunks.title: Agent

chunks.heading: Saved prompts
chunks.text: Type / to run a slash command. Use this for work you repeat: a commit message, a PR checklist, a test pass.
chunks.title: Agent

chunks.heading: After a change
chunks.text: Every file edit shows a diff in the thread. 1. Read the diff. 2. Keep it, skip it, or say what to change. 3. Repeat until the thread is done. BetterShape does not push to GitHub on its own. See Commits when you want a commit.
chunks.title: Agent

chunks.heading: New chat
chunks.text: Start a new chat when the topic changes. A long thread about one bug will confuse a later request about a different feature. Ctrl+Shift+L opens a new chat.
chunks.title: Agent

chunks.heading: Outside accounts
chunks.text: Chat can use a connected plugin (GitHub, Slack, Linear, and similar) or a local MCP server. Connect those first, then mention the task in the message.
chunks.title: Agent

chunks.text: Use Plan when the work is large enough that you want to see the steps first. A rename in one file does not need Plan. A new settings page across several files does.
chunks.title: Plan

chunks.heading: What it writes
chunks.text: Plan writes the approach into .bettershape/plans/ and shows it in the thread. It does not start editing until you continue. The plan is a file you can read and change. If a step is wrong, fix it in the thread before you build.
chunks.title: Plan

chunks.heading: How to run it
chunks.text: 1. Switch the composer to Plan . 2. Describe the change in the same way you would in Code. Include the goal, the files you know about, and anything that must not change. 3. Wait for the plan in the thread. 4. Edit the plan if a step is off. Say which step and why. 5. Continue when you want BetterShape to build it. If you already know the change is one file, skip Plan and use Code.
chunks.title: Plan

chunks.heading: What to put in the request
chunks.text: Good Plan prompts name the outcome and the limits: “Add a password field to account settings. Do not change billing.” “Split the homepage hero into its own component. Keep the current copy.” Weak prompts skip the limit. BetterShape will fill in the blanks, and you will spend a turn undoing that.
chunks.title: Plan

chunks.heading: After you continue
chunks.text: Building uses the plan as the checklist. If the implementation drifts, say so in the same thread. Start a new Plan only if the goal itself changed. When the build is done, read the diffs the same way you would after Code. Keep or skip each file. Commit when you are ready. See Commits.
chunks.title: Plan

chunks.text: Use Review when something is broken, or when a change feels risky and you want a second look. It is not for rewriting a feature. The Review mark in the composer is the purple mask icon. There is no separate Debug mode.
chunks.title: Review

chunks.heading: What it does
chunks.text: Review looks for the cause first, then proposes a small fix. You still keep or skip the diff. It works best when you give it a signal: A stack trace from the terminal. A failing test name. @ on the file that throws. The last change you made, in one sentence. “It doesn’t work” is not enough. BetterShape will guess, and the guess is often the wrong file.
chunks.title: Review

chunks.heading: How to run it
chunks.text: 1. Switch the composer to Review . 2. Paste the error or point at the file. 3. Read the finding in the thread. It should name the cause, not only restyle the code. 4. Keep the fix if it is small and correct. Skip it if it refactors past the bug.
chunks.title: Review

chunks.heading: After a large edit
chunks.text: After a multi file change, you can run Review on the same thread and ask it to list what is actually wrong. That still lands as diffs you can keep or skip. Do not use Review as a formatter. If you want tests written, say that in Code . If you want a second pass on a pull request, say which PR. See GitHub.
chunks.title: Review

chunks.text: Use the in app browser when you want to edit the live page instead of describing the UI in chat. This is not the same as Visual mode in the composer. Visual mode asks the agent to design. The browser lets you click the page in front of you.
chunks.title: Browser

chunks.heading: Start the page
chunks.text: 1. Run your app the way you usually do ( npm run dev , and so on). 2. Copy the local URL (for example http://localhost:3000 ). 3. Open that URL in BetterShape’s browser. This works with Next.js, Vite, Astro, and Remix. The app has to be running. BetterShape does not start it for you. If the preview cannot reach localhost, the dev server is not up, or it is bound to another host. See troubleshooting.
chunks.title: Browser

chunks.heading: Edit the page
chunks.text: Select an element and change it. BetterShape writes the same change into the source. You still review the diff in the thread. Keep it if the source matches what you changed on the page. Skip it if it touched the wrong file.
chunks.title: Browser

chunks.heading: What to expect
chunks.text: Layout and copy changes map cleanly when the element is in one component. Shared components update every screen that uses them. That is correct. Read the diff before you keep it. Styles that come from a design token may change the token, not a one off class.
chunks.title: Browser

chunks.heading: Chat on the side
chunks.text: You can still send a Visual or Code message while the browser is open. Say which screen you have open if the app has more than one route. When you are done, go back to Code for logic that is not on the page.
chunks.title: Browser

chunks.text: Every turn re sends the whole thread to the model: your messages, the agent's answers, and every tool result. The context window is finite, so a long thread runs out of room eventually. Input gets truncated, and BetterShape seems to forget what you said an hour ago. A short chat never hits the limit. A long one does, and it helps to know what survives.
chunks.title: Context and compaction

chunks.heading: What happens, in order
chunks.text: 1. Tool output is trimmed. Old tool results shrink to a head and tail excerpt. A result the model no longer needs, such as an older read of a file it read again later, becomes a one line note. 2. Older turns are summarized. Past roughly 74% of the window, BetterShape folds the older turns into one summary and keeps the newest turns word for word. That is compaction. 3. The summary is reused. After the first fold, later turns send the summary plus the recent turns instead of the whole transcript, so BetterShape does not re summarize on every message. 4. Oversized output goes to disk. A single tool result too big for the budget is written under .bettershape/agent out/ and the model gets the path.
chunks.title: Context and compaction

chunks.heading: Run it yourself
chunks.text: Manual compaction uses the same engine as the automatic pass, so a thread you compacted by hand keeps working the same way. The agent can also compact mid task when a turn is running long.
chunks.title: Context and compaction

chunks.heading: What the summary keeps
chunks.text: The summary follows a fixed outline rather than a free form recap: The request and the intent, including anything you ruled out. Technical concepts and the shape of the solution. Files and code sections, with the important snippets. Errors, fixes, and rejected approaches. Problems solved and the state of the work. Every user message, so early instructions survive. Work in progress and the next step. BetterShape also re attaches the five most recently read or written files, so the agent picks up where it left off instead of re reading them. Want every summary to carry something specific? An API shape, a set of migration names, a house tone? Write it once in Settings → Agents → Instructions → Compaction. Those instructions are appended to every compaction, manual or automatic.
chunks.title: Context and compaction

chunks.heading: When the agent slows compaction down
chunks.text: Automatic compaction picks its moment from a token count, and a token count cannot tell whether the agent is half way through a rename across six files. When it is, the agent can hold the automatic pass. It calls compact context on its own, with a one line reason: That call is the hold, not a summary of the work. The reason is pinned into the next summary, so the thing it was protecting survives the fold. A hold is bounded, because an unbounded one would let the window overflow, and a truncated window loses more than a summary does: It lapses after about 15 minutes, or 16k tokens of growth, or 3 skipped passes. It is overridden when the chat reaches about 92% of the window. It is checked before every model call in a turn, not only between turns. A single run of work can take hundreds of tool calls, and a window that fills up in the middle of one fails the call outright, so the check happens mid turn too. /compact from you always works, and a finished turn clears the hold. A fold is saved as it happens, so a summary survives a restart and a reopened chat does not send the raw history again. Only the part no summary covers yet is sent to be summarized, and the previous summary is handed in as the base. Settings → Agents → Context shows the hold, its reason, and a Compact now button while one is active.
chunks.title: Context and compaction

chunks.heading: What you still see
chunks.text: Compaction changes what the model reads, not what you keep. The earlier messages stay in the chat, with a marker where the summary took over. The pre compaction transcript is archived under .bettershape/agent out/ , so the agent can grep it when a detail is missing. Each chat keeps its own summary. Opening another thread, or starting a new one, starts from that thread's history. Settings → Agents → Context shows what compaction has done in the open chat: how many passes, how many tokens it freed. Reset goes back to sending the raw transcript, and since nothing was deleted, nothing is lost.
chunks.title: Context and compaction

chunks.heading: When compaction does not run
chunks.text: Incognito chats are never summarized. If the summary call fails, or the result is too short to be useful, BetterShape leaves the thread alone and retries later. It will not silently drop turns. "Nothing to compact yet" means the thread is still small enough to send whole.
chunks.title: Context and compaction

chunks.text: Plugins let chat use GitHub, Slack, Linear, Stripe, and similar accounts. You connect the account once, then mention the task in a message. Plugins run through your own Composio account. Add its API key in Settings → Agents → Plugins first (composio.com → API keys). A tool that runs on your machine is MCP.
chunks.title: Plugins

chunks.heading: Connect an account
chunks.text: 1. Open Settings → Agents → Plugins . 2. Pick the service. 3. Sign in in the browser window and allow access. 4. Return to BetterShape. You can disconnect from the same place. Disconnecting stops new chat turns from using that account. It does not delete past threads.
chunks.title: Plugins

chunks.heading: Use it in chat
chunks.text: Say what you need in plain language. You do not need a special syntax. Examples: “Open a pull request for this branch.” “List my Linear issues tagged bug.” “Post a summary of this diff to the engineering Slack channel.” If the plugin is not connected, BetterShape cannot call it. Connect it first, then send the message again.
chunks.title: Plugins

chunks.heading: GitHub in two places
chunks.text: Signing in for GitHub loads pull requests and related data for the open folder. A GitHub plugin is for chat. You may need both, depending on what you are doing.
chunks.title: Plugins

chunks.heading: If it fails
chunks.text: Sign in again. Check that the account has access to the repo or workspace you named. Then send a shorter message that names the repo or channel.
chunks.title: Plugins

chunks.text: MCP servers are tools BetterShape can call from chat. Add one in Settings → Agents → MCP , or keep a server in mcp.json if you want it in a file. Servers you add in Settings stay in BetterShape. They are not written into mcp.json . A server in mcp.json is picked up on its own. You do not have to add it again in Settings. Use MCP when the tool runs on your machine or at a URL you already have. Use a plugin when the tool is an outside account.
chunks.title: MCP

chunks.heading: Add a server in Settings
chunks.text: Open Settings → Agents → MCP and choose Add server . There are two tabs. Browse the registry searches the official MCP registry, the same index the agent searches. Search for a product or package name, check the command shown under a result, then choose Install . BetterShape writes the entry to mcp.json and connects it, so the server is there after a restart. If it needs a sign in, BetterShape opens the browser flow. Paste a config takes a server URL or a JSON config. Servers added this way stay in BetterShape and are not written to mcp.json . Remove a server you added by pasting with Remove . That does not change mcp.json .
chunks.title: MCP

chunks.heading: Open the file
chunks.text: On the MCP page, choose Open mcp.json . If the file does not exist yet, BetterShape creates it.
chunks.title: MCP

chunks.heading: Add a server
chunks.text: Use command when BetterShape should start the process. Use url if the server is already running. Save the file. Name the server something you will recognize in chat. The name is what you will refer to, not the package name.
chunks.title: MCP

chunks.heading: Try it
chunks.text: Send a message that needs the tool. If the server does not show up: 1. Save mcp.json . 2. Open Settings → Agents → MCP again. BetterShape reloads the file. 3. Open the same folder again. 4. Check that command is on your PATH when BetterShape starts. A tool that only works in your existing terminal session will fail here.
chunks.title: MCP

chunks.heading: Let the agent manage servers
chunks.text: You do not have to open Settings for this. Ask in chat, and BetterShape can add, change, test, or remove a server for you. The tools are mcp manage (server lifecycle) and mcp search / mcp call (using the tools a server exposes). The agent can: List servers and their status. Search the registry for a server by name, then add it from the registry entry. Add, update, enable, disable, or remove a server, with command / args / env for a local process or url / headers for a remote one. Test a server and report the tool count and latency. A test that passes saves the server unless you pass save: false . Start sign in for a server that needs OAuth. List the tools a server exposes. Servers the agent creates are written to the same mcp.json the Settings page reads, so they show up there too. Pass save: false to add a server for the current session only. Adding a server changes which tools BetterShape can call, so a mode that only reads will not do it. Approve the action like any other edit. A local server is a program this machine will run, so the first time one is added, updated, or tested, BetterShape asks for approval in the chat and shows the exact command. Servers already in mcp.json , and everything you add yourself in Settings, are past that point. Set Auto run to Always in Settings to stop the questions.
chunks.title: MCP

chunks.heading: Headers
chunks.text: Remote servers that authenticate with a header use headers : BetterShape sends those headers on every request to that server. When the server uses OAuth instead, BetterShape does not send a stored Authorization header — the OAuth token wins.
chunks.title: MCP

chunks.heading: Let the agent manage servers
chunks.text: You do not have to open Settings for this. Ask in chat, and BetterShape can add, change, test, or remove a server for you. The tools are mcp manage (server lifecycle) and mcp search / mcp call (using the tools a server exposes). The agent can: List servers and their status. Search the registry for a server by name, then add it from the registry entry. Add, update, enable, disable, or remove a server, with command / args / env for a local process or url / headers for a remote one. Test a server and report the tool count and latency. A test that passes saves the server unless you pass save: false . Start sign in for a server that needs OAuth. List the tools a server exposes. Servers the agent creates are written to the same mcp.json the Settings page reads, so they show up there too. Pass save: false to add a server for the current session only. Adding a server changes which tools BetterShape can call, so a mode that only reads will not do it. Approve the action like any other edit. A local server is a program this machine will run, so the first time one is added, updated, or tested, BetterShape asks for approval in the chat and shows the exact command. Servers already in mcp.json , and everything you add yourself in Settings, are past that point. Set Auto run to Always in Settings to stop the questions.
chunks.title: MCP

chunks.heading: Headers
chunks.text: Remote servers that authenticate with a header use headers : BetterShape sends those headers on every request to that server. When the server uses OAuth instead, BetterShape does not send a stored Authorization header — the OAuth token wins.
chunks.title: MCP

chunks.heading: The file on this machine
chunks.text: mcp.json lives in BetterShape’s data folder, not in the repo. Do not put API keys in it. Use env vars the server already reads.
chunks.title: MCP

chunks.heading: Remove a server
chunks.text: Delete the entry from mcp.json and save. Restart BetterShape if the tool still appears.
chunks.title: MCP

chunks.text: A slash command is a name plus a prompt you reuse. Type / in chat to pick one. Use this for work you do the same way every time: writing a commit message, checking a PR, generating tests in a fixed shape.
chunks.title: Slash commands

chunks.heading: Add one
chunks.text: 1. Open Settings → Agents → Workflows . 2. Give it a short name. That name is what you type after / . 3. Write the prompt you want BetterShape to follow. Be specific about the output: a commit message, a list of risks, a test file, and so on. 4. Save it. Keep the prompt as the instructions, not as a one off about the current branch. The current project still comes from the open folder and the thread.
chunks.title: Slash commands

chunks.heading: Run one
chunks.text: Type / in the composer and choose the command. You can add extra text after it, such as /commit focus on the billing page . A trigger phrase in a normal message can run it too, if you set one on the command.
chunks.title: Slash commands

chunks.heading: What to put in the prompt
chunks.text: Write it like you would brief a person who has never seen this repo: What to look at ( @ files, or “the diff in source control”). What to produce. What to avoid (“do not change snapshots”). Bad commands are one word. “Review” with no standard is not a command. The Review mode already exists.
chunks.title: Slash commands

chunks.heading: Edit or delete
chunks.text: Open Settings → Agents → Workflows again. Change the prompt, or delete the command. Existing threads do not change. Skills (reusable instructions the agent can load) live under Settings → Agents → Skills . They are separate from slash commands.
chunks.title: Slash commands

chunks.heading: Built-in commands
chunks.text: BetterShape ships a few commands that are not prompts. They run locally and never reach the model. Command What it does /compact [focus] Summarize the earlier part of the thread and keep going.
chunks.title: Slash commands

chunks.heading: /compact
chunks.text: Long threads eventually fill the model's context window. /compact folds the older turns into one summary, keeps the newest turns verbatim, and continues in the same thread. Use it when: The thread is long and BetterShape starts forgetting things you said earlier. You finished a stage of work and want to start the next one without the old noise. A request failed because the context was too long. Add a focus to steer the summary: /compact keep the migration plan and the API shapes . Without a focus, BetterShape uses your standing compaction instructions from Settings → Agents → Instructions → Compaction . BetterShape also compacts on its own when a thread gets close to the window limit, so you rarely have to run this. The summary is the record of what was folded — everything before it stays in the transcript for you to scroll, and older turns are not deleted from the thread. See Context and compaction for what is kept and what is dropped.
chunks.title: Slash commands

chunks.text: BetterShape does not commit when it edits a file. You keep or skip the diff in chat first. Then you commit what is actually on disk.
chunks.title: Commits

chunks.heading: From chat
chunks.text: In Code mode, ask it to commit. Name the files if you only want some of them. Read the message it drafts before you let it run. This uses the open folder’s git repo. Open the repo root, not a nested package, unless that package is its own repo.
chunks.title: Commits

chunks.heading: From the terminal
chunks.text: Open the terminal ( Ctrl+ ) and run git the way you usually do. Stage, commit, and push from there if you prefer.
chunks.title: Commits

chunks.heading: Commit graph
chunks.text: View → Git Manager opens the commit graph in the workspace. Use it to see history on the current folder.
chunks.title: Commits

chunks.heading: Remotes and GitHub
chunks.text: A GitHub login is only needed for remotes hosted on GitHub, pull requests, issues, and Actions. Local commits work without it. See GitHub.
chunks.title: Commits

chunks.heading: After an agent edit
chunks.text: Keep or skip the diffs in the chat thread first. Then commit what is actually in the working tree. Skipping a diff in chat and committing the same file from disk will still include that file if it is still changed on disk.
chunks.title: Commits

chunks.text: Sign in with GitHub when the open folder has a github.com remote. This login is separate from the account you use for chat. A local only repo has nothing to load from GitHub.
chunks.title: GitHub

chunks.heading: Sign in
chunks.text: Open a pull request from the workspace, or ask chat after you connect the GitHub plugin. Finish the browser step, then return to BetterShape. If data is missing, sign in again, and confirm the open folder is the repo you think it is ( git remote v in the terminal).
chunks.title: GitHub

chunks.heading: Open a pull request
chunks.text: 1. Commit and push the branch. See Commits. 2. Open a pull request from BetterShape, or ask chat to open one if the GitHub plugin is connected. 3. Read the title and body. BetterShape can draft them from the branch. You confirm before it is published. Do not publish a PR for a folder that is not the repo you meant to open.
chunks.title: GitHub

chunks.heading: Chat vs GitHub login
chunks.text: Asking chat to “open a PR” uses a plugin if you connected one. GitHub login is for the open folder’s github.com remote. Use whichever matches the task.
chunks.title: GitHub

chunks.heading: Sign out
chunks.text: Sign out of GitHub from the same place you signed in. Chat is unaffected — it uses your model provider keys.
chunks.title: GitHub

chunks.text: BetterShape is a desktop app for Windows 10 or 11, 64 bit. There is no browser only editor. You download the app, then open a folder on disk.
chunks.title: Install

chunks.heading: Download
chunks.text: 1. Get the installer from GitHub releases. 2. Run it. 3. If Windows SmartScreen appears, choose More info , then Run anyway . 4. Open BetterShape from the Start menu. If the installer will not run, you are on 32 bit Windows, or the download was cut short. Download it again.
chunks.title: Install

chunks.heading: Add a model provider after install
chunks.text: There is no account to create and nothing to sign in to. BetterShape has no server of its own, so chat runs once you supply a model key yourself. 1. Open Settings , then Providers . 2. Add a key for OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google — or any OpenAI compatible endpoint. 3. Pick a default model under Settings , then AI . Until a usable provider is configured, the composer stays disabled and says so. Everything else — opening files, editing, git, terminal — works without one.
chunks.title: Install

chunks.heading: Updates
chunks.text: This build has no update feed. Help → Check for Updates contacts no server. If you need a newer version, download a fresh installer from GitHub releases and run it over the existing install.
chunks.title: Install

chunks.heading: Uninstall
chunks.text: Uninstall from Windows Settings like any other desktop app. Your project files on disk are not deleted. Local BetterShape data for the app may remain under your user folder.
chunks.title: Install

chunks.heading: Next
chunks.text: Open a folder and send a task.
chunks.title: Install

chunks.text: These are the defaults. Change them in Settings → Application → Keyboard Shortcuts . Action Shortcut Open folder Ctrl+K Ctrl+O Show or hide chat Ctrl+L New chat Ctrl+Shift+L Command palette Ctrl+Shift+P Go to file Ctrl+P Terminal Ctrl+ Settings Ctrl+, Design mode (in app browser) Ctrl+Shift+D Cycle Code / Ask / Plan Ctrl+Shift+.
chunks.title: Shortcuts

chunks.heading: How to change one
chunks.text: Open Settings → Application → Keyboard Shortcuts and assign a new chord. If the key is taken, pick another or clear the old one.
chunks.title: Shortcuts

chunks.heading: Chord vs one key
chunks.text: Open folder is two steps: Ctrl+K , then Ctrl+O . Wait for the chord, then press the second part. If you only press Ctrl+K , you are waiting for the follow up.
chunks.title: Shortcuts

chunks.heading: Chat
chunks.text: Ctrl+L shows or hides the chat sidebar. Click the composer (or start a new chat) when you want to type.
chunks.title: Shortcuts

chunks.heading: Can I work offline?
chunks.text: Editing files, search, and the terminal work without a connection. Chat and Git push/pull need one.
chunks.title: FAQ

chunks.heading: Is there a free tier or a credit balance?
chunks.text: No. BetterShape has no account, no plan, and no credits. You pay your model provider directly for what you use.
chunks.title: FAQ

chunks.heading: Does BetterShape upload my project?
chunks.text: Not by default. Chat sends the files and context you include in a turn, plus what the agent reads to do the task. Local editing does not require chat.
chunks.title: FAQ

chunks.heading: Can I use my own model key?
chunks.text: That is the only way chat works. Add a key in Settings → Providers — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI compatible endpoint. Nothing is proxied through a server we run.
chunks.title: FAQ

chunks.heading: What OS is supported?
chunks.text: Windows 10 or 11, 64 bit. See Install.
chunks.title: FAQ

chunks.heading: Is there anything to sign in to?
chunks.text: No. There is no BetterShape account. The only credentials in the app are the provider keys you add and the Git host login you use for push and pull.
chunks.title: FAQ

chunks.text: Start with the matching heading. If none of these fit, contact with the version from Help → About .
chunks.title: Troubleshooting

chunks.heading: The app will not open
chunks.text: It needs Windows 10 or 11, 64 bit. Download the installer again from GitHub releases and run it. If it opens and closes immediately, run it once more after a reboot. If it still fails, send the version you tried to install.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting

chunks.heading: Chat says no provider is configured
chunks.text: Open Settings → Providers and add an API key. BetterShape calls the provider directly with that key; there is no account to sign in to. If a key is set and send still fails, the provider returned the error — the status line under the message names the provider and the HTTP status.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting

chunks.heading: A model does not appear in the menu
chunks.text: The menu lists the models offered by presets, plus anything in Extra models on the provider card. Add the id by hand if your provider serves a model we do not list.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting

chunks.heading: The preview cannot reach localhost
chunks.text: Start your app first, then open that URL in the browser. localhost has to be the same machine. A URL on another device will not load in BetterShape’s preview.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting

chunks.heading: GitHub data is missing
chunks.text: Sign in with GitHub and open a folder whose remote is on github.com. A fork or an org the GitHub account cannot see will look empty.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting

chunks.heading: MCP tools do not appear
chunks.text: Save mcp.json , restart BetterShape, and open the folder again. The command has to exist on PATH for the app, not only for a terminal you already opened. See MCP.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting

chunks.heading: An update did not apply
chunks.text: Use Help → Check for Updates . This build has no update feed, so if it still reports the old version, install over it from GitHub releases.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting

chunks.text: Product questions go to contact. Include: The version from Help → About . What you tried, and what happened instead. Do not send API keys, provider tokens, or a dump of .env files.
chunks.title: Contact

chunks.heading: Billing
chunks.text: There is nothing to bill here: BetterShape has no account and no subscription. Model usage is billed by the provider whose key you added.
chunks.title: Contact

chunks.heading: Security
chunks.text: Security issues go through SECURITY.md on GitHub. Do not file those as a normal product question.
chunks.title: Contact

chunks.heading: Status
chunks.text: If a provider's API is down, check that provider's status page before you write in.
chunks.title: Contact
